results.title: Maria Luisa de la Puerta Fernández - Researcher, Project Manager, and Grant Writer. ICT & Machine Learning Advocate - Mie University
results.content:
Maria Luisa de la Puerta Fernández
Researcher, Project Manager, and Grant Writer. ICT & Machine Learning Advocate
Tsu, Mie, Japan
500 connections, 1515 followers


About
Experienced researcher and consultant specializing in sustainable intensification, food security, and One Health initiatives. I focus on leveraging ICT and machine learning for innovation in the livestock sector and agroforestry. With extensive experience in Sub-Saharan Africa and other global regions, I excel at connecting academia, industry, and policymakers for scalable solutions. Passionate about enhancing productivity while ensuring environmental sustainability and community well-being.


Experience
JSPS Research Fellow
[Mie University](https://jp.linkedin.com/company/mie-university)  
Apr 2025 - Present
Japan
As a JSPS Fellow, I will leverage my interdisciplinary expertise in animal nutrition, data science, and business insight to enhance livestock management through innovative machine learning tools. Building on my PhD research in sustainable animal nutrition and the projects I have supported through my company, Omeva Consulting, I aim to support the development of an AI-model to predict starch digestibility in cattle. This tool will empower farmers to make data-driven decisions, reduce feed costs, and optimise cattle nutrition using locally available resources.Key skills I bring include:•	Strong analytical and experimental design skills for developing robust datasets to train AI models•	Expertise in developing business solutions for the livestock sector, focusing on user friendly tools•	Insight into Python, Google Colab, and data analysis for agricultural applications•	Machine learning model development, such as EfficientNet v2 and YOLOv8 for predictive analysis•	Proven ability to secure funding and build relationships with public and private stakeholders•	Strong communication and project management skills, facilitating collaboration across teams and countriesThis research will contribute to Japan’s agricultural sustainability by promoting locally sourced feed ingredients such as rice and providing farmers with an accessible tool to optimise feed efficiency. It aligns with my broader ambition to bridge research, technology, and business development in agriculture through practical, user-focused solutions. In addition to my technical role, I look forward to engaging with Japanese stakeholders, farmers, researchers, and businesses, to ensure the tool’s relevance and long-term impact. Drawing on my experience in cross-cultural communication and international collaboration, I aim to build meaningful partnerships both locally and globally. I am also committed to strengthening my Japanese language skills to foster deeper engagement throughout the fellowship.


Education
Aberystwyth University
Doctor of Philosophy - PhD, Animal Nutrition
2018 - 2024
After several years of doing a PhD while working as a researcher, I decided to go for a full time PhD position at Aberystwyth University, UK. I am working on the role of enhancers in silage microbiota, especially on their effects on spoilage yeast.
